Variance and covariance chapter

Variance and covariance: scientific and visual review

Delivery status and source synthesis

Quality-reviewed English draft; student approval is not inferred. Eighteen substantive teaching sections precede a complete-sentence summary, 87 worked problem entries, 80 final reasoning rules and 23 concept-specific models. The evaluated pool contains nine universities. MIT, CMU, Oxford and Berkeley form the four core written courses; ETH Zurich and Cornell supply genuinely read extensions. Stanford, Harvard and Cambridge are screened candidates, not counted as read. The source audit identifies exact page ranges, identities, acquisition hashes, gaps and corrections. This is a documented bounded search, not a claim to have read every course in existence.

Mathematical review

Independent checks cover all 169 stored checkpoints, 414 enumeration cases and 162 inputs to the actual editable JavaScript calculator. The reference methods enumerate permutations, without-replacement subsets and random-walk paths, derive moments from rational raw sums, integrate the printed MIT cubic joint density symbolically, and evaluate covariance quadratic forms independently. Duplicate-valued and degenerate atoms are included. Correlation is undefined when either variance is zero. Coincident scatter markers combine probability mass while the signed contribution ledger retains separate input atoms.

The manuscript states square-integrability conditions, distinguishes affine from nonlinear transformations, handles shared randomness, retains all cross terms and separates conditional independence from marginal independence. It proves the constant-predictor and linear-predictor identities, total variance and covariance, positive semidefiniteness, the Gaussian exception, Markov/Chebyshev/Cantelli bounds and Welford's recurrence. It treats sharpness, null conditioning events, sampling fractions, fixed-point n=1, endpoint equality, singular covariance matrices, rate versus scale, tail events and numerical cancellation explicitly.

Native MathML parsing and fence review passed all 713 static expressions; the mounted page contains 760 expressions including player panels. No unmatched delimiters or closing-fence-only script bases were detected. The review documents and independently corrects several source-example errors rather than silently copying them.

Worked questions and final notes

There are 84 independently authored or reconstructed formula/concept questions and three authentic Iranian examination entries. PhD CS 1405 questions 58 and 59 and MS CE 1405 question 36 were inspected on the original rendered PDF pages. The first and third are explicitly revisited items, not new unique questions. Paths, immutable repository commit, PDF hashes, printed alternative order and derived answers are recorded. No official answer key is claimed.

The bank covers moment recovery, transformation and centering, joint densities, covariance expansions, correlation feasibility, indicator counts, overlapping events, sampling, shared latent variables, conditional decomposition, prediction, matrix certificates, bounds, distributions, generating functions and numerical implementation. Every solution provides a derivation with complete sentences. The 80 final rules state their assumptions and common wrong inferences. Visual decisions are recorded for every entry: a relevant model is attached when a law or causal transition aids the solution; a pure algebraic certificate is not decorated with an unrelated animation.

Visual and browser review

Real Edge checked every stored checkpoint across 23 distinct models and 47 embedded player placements. It checked text bounds and padding, geometry, native mathematics, loaded fonts, actual movement, in-flight pause/resume, before/result comparison, seeking, restart, reduced motion, printable checkpoints, five editable examples, eight invalid-input preservation cases, mobile containment and the library/week-four links. The browser report passed with no runtime errors. Representative covariance, mixture, matrix, permutation, mobile and mass-transfer screenshots were inspected.

The compact 760 by 360 drawings have subject-specific representations: probability-weighted squared distances, true-coordinate scatter and signed covariance, conditional within/between contributions, sampling laws, permutation fixed points, risk quadratics, averaging curves and exact random-walk mass transfers. Random-walk arrows connect source and destination circle boundaries. Each branch sends only its probability-weighted source mass; the partial destination is explicitly not normalized and completed moments are updated only after both branches of every source atom have arrived. Markers with coincident coordinates aggregate their probability area. Standard-deviation intervals are explicitly not complete supports.

Headings use Newsreader; prose uses Source Sans 3; code uses JetBrains Mono; mathematics and mathematical labels use STIX Two Math. Captions identify rounding and plot scaling. Exact checkpoint data remain inspectable.

Retention, publication and limits

All 56 preceding delivered chapter HTML files passed byte-for-byte retention. A stale pre-final-render hash for the amortized chapter was reconciled against its actual immutable delivered Git source; the chapter itself was unchanged. See baseline-reconciliation.json. The resulting library contains 57 chapters and 3913 worked problem entries. Online deployment is tracked separately from local and GitHub completeness.

These finite audits and selected symbolic proofs do not certify universal correctness or performance on every unseen examination question. The bank does not reproduce every copyrighted exercise in the source courses. Full distribution catalogues, estimation theory and measure-theoretic constructions belong to later chapters; their necessary second-moment interfaces are taught here. Remaining uncertainty is disclosed rather than labeled as a literal 100-percent guarantee.
